Students in a biology class investigated why individual house mice (Mus musculus) can differ from one another in their susceptibility to cataracts in old age. The students compared wild-type mice and knockout mice, which are mice with specific genes deactivated, when mice of each type were raised in similar naturalistic environments and periodically tested for cataracts. Finding that knockout mice with the gene Aasdh deactivated tended to develop cataracts more frequently than did wild-type mice, the students concluded that differences in cataract frequency among house mice in nature are solely attributable to variations in the level of expression of Aasdh.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the students' conclusion?
choices: Some wild-type mice were very similar to the knockout mice with regard to cataract frequency but showed a wide variety of levels of expression of Aasdh.
The level of expression of Aasdh does not appear to affect the functioning of any other genes in house mice.
A sampling of house mice captured in natural settings shows that individual mice can differ from one another in the level of expression of Aasdh.
The mice with Aasdh deactivated were identical to the wild-type mice except with regard to cataract frequency.
explanation:
Step 1: What is the students’ conclusion?

The students conclude:

Differences in cataract frequency among house mice in nature are solely attributable to differences in the level of expression of Aasdh.

Key word: solely
That means only Aasdh expression explains the differences. No other factor matters.

Step 2: What evidence do they use?

Knockout mice (Aasdh deactivated) develop cataracts more frequently than wild-type mice.

Mice were raised in similar environments.

From this, they jump to a strong causal claim about natural variation in cataracts.

Step 3: What would weaken that conclusion?

To weaken it, we need evidence that:

Cataract frequency does not reliably track Aasdh expression, or

Something other than Aasdh expression can explain cataract differences.

Step 4: Why A weakens the conclusion

A.
Some wild-type mice were very similar to the knockout mice with regard to cataract frequency but showed a wide variety of levels of expression of Aasdh.

This directly attacks the core assumption:

If mice have similar cataract rates but very different Aasdh expression levels, then Aasdh expression cannot be the sole cause of cataract frequency.

In short:
Same outcome (cataracts)
Different Aasdh levels
→ Aasdh expression alone doesn’t explain cataracts

That directly undermines the word solely in the conclusion.

Step 5: Why the other choices do NOT weaken

B.
Says Aasdh expression does not affect other genes.
This doesn’t challenge the claim that Aasdh affects cataracts. Neutral.

C.
Just says mice vary in Aasdh expression in nature.
That actually supports the idea that expression differences exist and could matter.

D.
Says knockout mice were identical to wild-type mice except for cataract frequency.
That strengthens the causal link instead of weakening it.

explanation:

The underlined text does two things:

Admits a potential flaw
– The Far Side of the World has a rather abrupt ending.

Immediately explains why that flaw may not actually be a flaw
– The next book picks up neatly where it leaves off, so the ending only feels abrupt if you read the book in isolation.

So the author is anticipating a criticism and then softening it.

Step 2: How does that fit into the passage as a whole?

The passage argues that the Aubrey/Maturin series should be viewed as:

a single long work, not

a set of fully independent novels.

The underlined portion supports this idea by explaining why the abrupt ending isn’t really a problem when the series is read as intended.

Step 3: Why A is correct

A.
It offers a detail that helps explain why it is not necessarily the case that a certain characteristic of The Far Side of the World should be considered a flaw.

“not necessarily a flaw” = explained by continuity with the next book

B.
Talks about engagement or how enjoyable the novels are.
The passage never discusses reader enjoyment.

question:
______ traditional descriptions of pollination syndromes (suites of floral traits, such as nectar composition and symmetry, hypothesized to have independently evolved as a result of selection pressure exerted by pollinators) and recent empirical observations of floral-trait combinations have led some ecologists to express reservations about the utility of those descriptions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Correct answer
Discrepancies between

Why this is correct
The sentence structure is:

“_____ traditional descriptions of pollination syndromes … and recent empirical observations of floral-trait combinations have led some ecologists to express reservations about the utility of those descriptions.”

Key logic:
• Traditional descriptions exist.
• Recent empirical observations exist.
• These two things do not line up.
• Because they do not line up, ecologists now question the usefulness of the traditional descriptions.

“Discrepancies between” directly signals a mismatch or conflict between two sets of ideas, which explains why reservations arise.

Grammatically, it also fits perfectly:
“Discrepancies between X and Y have led…”

Why the other choices are wrong

Proclamations of
• “Proclamations” means declarations or announcements.
• The sentence needs a relationship between traditional descriptions and recent observations, not a label for one side alone.
• This choice removes the contrast that explains the ecologists’ reservations.

Recurrences of
• “Recurrences” means repeated appearances of the same thing.
• The passage is not saying old ideas are repeating; it’s saying they conflict with new evidence.
• This choice implies similarity over time, which contradicts the idea of doubt or reservation.

Affinities between
• “Affinities” means similarities or natural connections.
• If there were affinities between the two, ecologists would feel more confident, not less.
• This choice directly contradicts the conclusion of skepticism.

question:
Although Grant Tavinor concludes that computer games are art by virtue of their forming a subcategory of fiction, and Berys Gaut similarly places them within the realm of cinema, neither approach adequately captures a central aspect of playing these games: when the player no longer attends to the narrative and is instead simply absorbed in the instrumentalities of gameplay. This is among the reasons philosopher C. Thi Nguyen contends that the work of computer game designers is in what he calls the medium of player agency, which the designer prescribes through rules and goals, and which elicits positive aesthetic experiences in the player who agrees to adopt it. choices: are helpful starting points for studying computer games as art, even though these frameworks are overly simplistic.
are useful for analyzing the narrative aspects of computer games, even if neither attempts to address player agency.

subsume computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.
explanation:
Correct answer
subsumes computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.

Why this is correct
Nguyen criticizes frameworks that treat games like fiction or cinema because they ignore player agency, which he argues is central to how games produce enjoyment.

Choice D directly captures this criticism: those frameworks misclassify games and fail to address an essential feature.

Why the other choices are wrong

Helpful starting points but overly simplistic.
• Nguyen explicitly argues they are inadequate, not merely simplistic.

Useful for analyzing narrative aspects.
• The criticism is broader than narrative; it concerns agency.

Overstate influence of fiction and cinema.
• This misrepresents the critique; influence is not the issue.

question:
Like all species of baleen whales, the common minke whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. In this way, baleen whales can eat up to 30 percent of their total mass per day. And while no one would call the common minke whale small—it can have a mass as high as 4,000 kg—it is one of the smaller baleen whales and is much smaller than the blue whale, which can weigh a whopping 150,000 kg and consume as much as 45,000 kg of krill per day.

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be concluded about krill consumption among common minke and blue whales?
choices: Most baleen whales include krill in their diets, but the common minke whale is less likely than the blue whale to do so.
The quantities of krill consumed by blue whales has made it difficult for common minke whales to find sufficient food.
The blue whale is able to eat more krill per day than the common minke whale is.
Both the common minke whale and the blue whale can eat as much as 45,000 kg of krill per day.
explanation:
Why C is correct:

The passage states that the blue whale can weigh up to 150,000 kg and can consume as much as 45,000 kg of krill per day. The common minke whale, by contrast, is much smaller, with a mass of up to 4,000 kg, and the passage does not attribute a similar level of daily krill consumption to it. Since baleen whales can eat up to 30 percent of their body mass per day, and the blue whale has a far greater mass, it is reasonable to conclude that the blue whale is able to eat more krill per day than the common minke whale.

Why the other answers are wrong
❌ A Wrong because: The passage states that all baleen whales feed on krill.

❌ B Wrong because: The passage does not discuss competition or food scarcity.

❌ D Wrong because: The 45,000-kg figure applies only to the blue whale.

Subject-Verb Agreement with Indefinite Subjects

When words such as everybody, each, neither, either, anyone, no one, anybody, and similar indefinite pronouns are used as the subject of a sentence, they are treated as singular subjects, and the verb must also be singular.

Explanation

• Indefinite pronouns like everybody, each, nobody, anyone, no one, and similar words refer to a singular entity, even if they sound plural.
• These words require a singular verb, regardless of the plural idea they might seem to express.

Examples and Explanations

1. Example with "Everybody"

• Sentence: Everybody loves Simon.
• Explanation: The word "everybody" refers to a singular group of people, but it is treated as a singular subject.
• Since it is singular, we use the singular verb "loves."
• Answer: Everybody loves Simon.

2. Example with "Each"

• Sentence: Each of the boys has an hour to respond.
• Explanation: "Each" is singular, so even though it refers to multiple candidates, it takes a singular verb ("has") in this sentence.
• Answer: Each of the boys has an hour to respond.

3. Example with "Neither"

• Sentence: Neither of the girls wants to respond.
• Explanation: "Neither" is a singular subject, even though it might refer to two candidates.
• The verb must agree with the singular subject, so we use "wants."
• Answer: Neither of the girls wants to respond.

Exceptions

1. When you have "Neither...nor..."

• When you have "Neither" without the "nor" then "Neither" will serve as a singular subject.
• But if you have "Neither' followed by "nor" then you will need to look at the noun that follows the "nor" and treat that as the subject.

• Example 1

• Neither the boy nor <u>the girls</u> (likes/like) chocolate.
• Here, "the girls" follows "nor" so the subject will be "the girls."

• Example 2

• Neither the girls nor <u>the boy</u> (likes/like) chocolate.
• Here, "the boy" follows "nor" so the subject will be "the boy."

2. The same exception rule applies for "Either...or..."

Key Takeaways

• Indefinite pronouns like everybody, everything, each, anyone, no one, and similar terms are treated as singular subjects.
• These subjects always take a singular verb.
• Even if the subject refers to multiple things (e.g., "everybody"), the subject is still considered singular in grammar, so the verb should be in its singular form.

question:
Antonia Olivia Dolan and colleagues had musicians and nonmusicians with clinically average hearing listen to recordings of nature sounds and music in popular genres like acoustic folk and funk and adjust the volume to optimize their listening enjoyment. The researchers found that for a given recording that a musician and nonmusician identified as their favorite among those included in the study, optimal volume tended to be higher for the musician than for the nonmusician. Thus, if a musician and nonmusician both identified Jose Gonzalez’s “Heartbeats” as their favorite recording and the musician preferred to listen to it at a volume of 82.2 decibels, the nonmusician would be expected to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: find listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels less enjoyable than listening to it at a lower volume.
prefer listening to other music at 82.2 decibels over listening to “Heartbeats” at that volume.
enjoy listening to the nature sounds at 82.2 decibels more than listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels.
not find it enjoyable to listen to any recordings at a volume as low as 82.2 decibels.
explanation:
The study found that when both a musician and nonmusician liked the same recording, the musician usually preferred a higher volume than the nonmusician.

So if the musician’s best volume is 82.2 decibels, the nonmusician would likely prefer that same song at a lower volume.

Correct Answer: A
A is correct because the nonmusician would be expected to find 82.2 decibels less enjoyable than a lower volume. The study says optimal volume tends to be lower for nonmusicians than for musicians.

Incorrect Answers:
B — The study does not compare preference for one song versus other music at the same volume.

C — The study does not say nonmusicians prefer nature sounds over music.

D — This is too extreme and opposite of the logic. The nonmusician may still enjoy recordings, but their optimal volume would likely be lower than 82.2 decibels.

question:

Hypothesizing that elevated sound levels affect foraging among narwhals, Tervo’s team compared narwhal diving behaviors in natural sound conditions with those behaviors in two human-caused sound exposure conditions—ship sounds and ship sounds coupled with sonic pulses. Both exposure conditions resulted in significant decreases in the number and target depth of deep dives (associated with foraging) relative to natural conditions. However, differences between diving behaviors in the two exposure types were negligible, a finding that could be attributed to the fact that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: narwhals forage at shallower depths in the presence of ship sounds alone than in the presence of ship sounds coupled with sonic pulses.
sonic pulses can be heard at significantly greater ocean depths than ship sounds can.
the narwhals weren’t as sensitive to human-caused sounds as the researchers had predicted.
ship sounds contribute so much to the overall sound level that the addition of sonic pulses has little effect on the narwhals’ auditory environment.
explanation:
The study found that both human-caused noise conditions caused similar decreases in foraging dives, even though one condition added sonic pulses.

If adding sonic pulses did not make much difference, then ship sounds alone must already have strongly affected the narwhals’ sound environment.

Correct Answer: D
D is correct because it explains why the two exposure conditions had similar effects. If ship sounds already contributed so much noise that adding sonic pulses barely changed what the narwhals heard, then their diving behavior would be similar in both conditions.

Incorrect Answers:
A — This says narwhals forage at shallower depths with ship sounds alone than with ship sounds plus sonic pulses, but the passage says differences between the two exposure types were negligible.

B — This would suggest sonic pulses should have a different or stronger effect, but the passage says the two conditions produced similar results.

C — This contradicts the passage because the narwhals did show significant behavioral changes in response to human-caused sound.

question:
Text 1
The poet Audre Lorde once claimed that poetry is the most inexpensive of art forms to practice. While people who pursue other art forms—sculpture, architecture, theater—require large blocks of uninterrupted time as well as money to complete their work, poets can write, as Lorde said, “between shifts, in the hospital pantry, on the subway, and on scraps of surplus paper.” So poets can make worthwhile art even if they must earn their living in another way.

Text 2
Any assessment of the state of contemporary poetry must reckon with the professionalization of the field. While it is possible in theory for anyone to publish in Poetry, Kenyon Review, or a similar major poetry outlet, many people who do so have professional training in poetry and extensive practice writing it, which requires time not often available to those who must also work full-time jobs. Thus, financial security indirectly affects which people become poets.

Based on the texts, how would Lorde (Text 1) most likely respond to the argument presented in Text 2?
choices: By indicating that those poets who publish in major poetry journals are most likely to be able to earn a living by writing poetry
By pointing out that people can produce valuable poetry in other circumstances than those described by the author of Text 2
By suggesting that those artists who specialize in more financially rewarding artistic forms are unlikely to also be successful as poets
By asserting that people often work full-time jobs in order to afford the professional training described in Text 2
explanation:
Text 2 argues that professional poetry often requires time, training, and financial security, while Text 1/Lorde argues poetry can still be created in limited time and ordinary working conditions.

Lorde would likely push back by saying valuable poetry can be made outside professional, financially secure settings.

Correct Answer: B
B is correct because Text 1 emphasizes that poets can write “between shifts,” “on the subway,” and on scraps of paper. So Lorde would likely argue that people can still produce worthwhile poetry even without the professional training, time, or financial security described in Text 2.

Incorrect Answers:
A — Text 1 does not say poets who publish in major journals can earn a living from poetry. It focuses on poetry being accessible even to people with other jobs.

C — Text 1 compares poetry with other art forms, but it does not say artists in more financially rewarding fields cannot succeed as poets.

D — Text 1 does not argue that people work full-time jobs to afford professional training. It says people can write poetry even while earning a living another way.

question:

(2017) showed that adding specific bacterial or fungal strains to soil can yield increased vitamin C in strawberry crops, Vanderburgh and team applied intact microbial communities gathered from ecologically distinct settings across Colorado, including areas of aspen grove and sagebrush, to mustard plants and evaluated the flavor compounds in the plants’ seeds. This ensured that the microbial conditions in their experiment would better reflect the variation and complexity of naturally occurring communities.

Based on the text, what is the most likely reason Vanderburgh and colleagues chose to avoid the method used in the strawberry study?
choices: The microbial community in the soil from the strawberry study affected plants’ nutrition, not their flavor chemistry.
The diversity of species of microorganisms in the soil from the strawberry study was already abnormally high before the researchers added further microorganisms.
The composition of microorganisms in the soil in the strawberry study may not have been representative of a naturally existing composition.
The microbial community in the soil from the strawberry study likely included similar species to those in wild soils.
explanation:
The passage contrasts two methods: one study added specific bacterial or fungal strains, while Vanderburgh used intact microbial communities from natural settings.

Vanderburgh likely avoided the earlier method because adding selected strains would not reflect the full complexity of naturally occurring soil microbial communities.

Correct Answer: C
C is correct because the text says Vanderburgh used intact microbial communities from distinct natural settings so the experiment would better reflect the “variation and complexity of naturally occurring communities.” This implies that the strawberry study’s method, adding specific strains, may have been less representative of natural microbial compositions.

Incorrect Answers:
A — The difference between nutrition and flavor chemistry is not the main reason they avoided the method. The passage emphasizes microbial community complexity, not the outcome being measured.

B — The passage does not say the strawberry study’s soil already had abnormally high microbial diversity.

D — This says the opposite of the needed idea. If the strawberry study’s soil already included similar species to wild soils, that would make it more naturally representative, not less.

question:

Which finding, if true, would most clearly be an exception to the pattern Blatt identified?
choices: The novels of Virginia Woolf, one of the most celebrated writers of the twentieth century, have an average of 116 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, while the novels of Jane Austen, one of the most celebrated writers of the nineteenth century, have an average of 128 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

William Faulkner’s classic novel The Sound and the Fury has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Faulkner’s novels in Blatt’s study, while F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel The Great Gatsby has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Fitzgerald’s novels in Blatt’s study.

D.H. Lawrence’s acclaimed novel Women in Love and novels by several genre fiction authors that many critics regard as lacking in artistic quality have a comparable number of -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

Whereas award-winning and best-selling novels have on average 114 and 115 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, respectively, fan fiction novels, which are frequently authored by nonprofessional authors, have on average 154 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.
explanation:
Logic: To be an exception, look for a highly regarded novel with many -ly adverbs or a poorly regarded novel with few -ly adverbs. That would break the positive correlation between avoiding -ly adverbs and literary merit.

A. Incorrect: It compares two acclaimed authors and doesn't contradict the overall pattern.
B. Incorrect: Both classic novels have the lowest adverb rates among their authors' works, supporting the pattern.
C. Correct: An acclaimed novel and low-quality novels having similar adverb rates contradicts the claimed correlation.
D. Incorrect: Fan fiction having more -ly adverbs than acclaimed novels supports the pattern.

question:
The early Australian railroad system of the 1800s was famously uncoordinated. Trains on the narrow gauge Mackay Railway line in Queensland couldn't travel on the Yarra Valley Railway in Victoria, which used broad gauge tracks, without performing time-consuming conversions. ______ historians refer to this complicated system as the “mixed gauge muddle.”

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The inability to travel between rail systems is the reason historians call the network the "mixed gauge muddle." The relationship is cause and effect.

A. Incorrect: The second sentence is not expressing similarity.
B. Correct: Hence shows that the nickname follows from the described problem.
C. Incorrect: There is no contrast.
D. Incorrect: The second sentence is not another example.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Extravehicular activities (EVAs) are activities performed outside a spacecraft by astronauts in outer space.
• EVAs are also known as spacewalks.
• Jerry Ross is a former US astronaut who has performed 9 spacewalks.
• The total time of Ross’s spacewalks was 58 hours and 32 minutes.
• Benjamin Alvin Drew is a former US astronaut who has performed 2 spacewalks.
• The total time of Drew’s spacewalks was 12 hours and 48 minutes.
The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the astronauts Ross and Drew. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Drew has spent less time performing spacewalks than Ross has.
Ross and Drew have each performed multiple spacewalks.
EVAs, also known as spacewalks, are activities done by astronauts outside a spacecraft.
Ross has performed spacewalks, but Drew has performed EVAs.
explanation:
B is correct.

The goal is to emphasize a similarity between Ross and Drew.

Choice B says:

Ross and Drew have each performed multiple spacewalks.

That shows what they have in common: both astronauts performed more than one spacewalk.

Why A is wrong:
A says Drew spent less time spacewalking than Ross. That emphasizes a difference, not a similarity.

Why C is wrong:
C defines EVAs/spacewalks, but it doesn’t compare Ross and Drew.

Why D is wrong:
EVAs and spacewalks mean the same thing, but the sentence uses “but,” which makes it sound like a contrast. It’s not the clearest way to show similarity.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Calida Garcia Rawles is an African American painter.
• She is known for her large-scale, hyperrealistic paintings depicting African American figures in water.
• The painting Lost in the Shuffle (36 × 24 in) depicts two young men with their arms outstretched floating in the bottom left and upper right corners of the canvas.
• Guardian (96 × 48 in) depicts a woman in a white dress floating in the center of the canvas.
• She paints the water with vivid blue colors, including sapphire blue and ultramarine.
• The mood in the paintings is serene.
Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize a difference between the two paintings?
choices: Among the many stunning works of Calida Garcia Rawles is Guardian, a serene 96-by-48-inch painting depicting a woman floating in a white dress in the vivid blue water.
Although the number of figures may differ, constant among Rawles’s hyperrealistic works is the serene mood that the paintings evoke.
Calida Garcia Rawles captures the water in paintings such as Lost in the Shuffle and Guardian in vivid hues of sapphire blue and ultramarine.
While some of Rawles’s works, such as Lost in the Shuffle, feature two figures in the composition, Guardian features one figure floating in the vivid blue water.
explanation:
The goal is to emphasize a difference between the two paintings.

Choice D does that clearly:

Lost in the Shuffle features two figures, while Guardian features one figure.

That is a direct difference between the two paintings.

Why A is not best:
A only describes Guardian. It does not compare Guardian to Lost in the Shuffle, so it does not emphasize a difference between the two paintings.

Why B is not best:
B starts with a difference, but then focuses on a similarity: both paintings have a serene mood.

Why C is not best:
C emphasizes a similarity: both paintings use vivid blue water colors.

So the answer should be D.

question:
"The Monster” is an 1898 story by Stephen Crane. In the story, the character of Jimmie is a young boy who has been scolded by his father for accidentally damaging a flower in his garden; Jimmie then looks for sympathy from Henry Johnson, the man responsible for the care of Jimmie’s father’s horses. Crane demonstrates Henry’s tendency towards such sympathy, writing, _____

Which quotation from “The Monster” most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “Henry would sometimes choose to absolutely repudiate [Jimmie’s behavior], and when Jimmie appeared in his shame would bully him most virtuously, preaching with assurance the precepts of [Jimmie’s father’s] creed, and pointing out to Jimmie all of his abominations.”

“Henry... could usually provide a sin to place himself on a footing with the disgraced one. Perhaps he would remember that he had forgotten to put the hitching-strap in the back of the buggy on some recent occasion, and had been reprimanded by [Jimmie’s father].”
“Henry personally conducted [Jimmie’s father] during the splendid journeys through the country roads, where farms spread on all sides, with sheep, cows, and other marvels abounding.”
“In regard to almost everything in life [Jimmie and Henry] seemed to have minds precisely alike.”
explanation:
The claim we need to prove is that Henry tends to show sympathy toward Jimmie when Jimmie is in trouble.

B works because Henry “could usually provide a sin” of his own, meaning he remembers something bad he also did so he can be on the same level as Jimmie. Instead of judging Jimmie, Henry makes Jimmie feel less alone by showing, “I’ve messed up too.” That is sympathy.

Why the others are wrong:

A says Henry sometimes rejects Jimmie’s behavior and lectures him. That shows criticism, not sympathy.

C is just about Henry driving Jimmie’s father through the country. It doesn’t show Henry comforting Jimmie.

D says Jimmie and Henry thought alike about many things. That shows similarity, but it doesn’t specifically show Henry being sympathetic when Jimmie is ashamed.

question:
The neurotechnology company Q30 Innovations is working on an exciting new technology: collars that increase blood volume in the brain to reduce potential damage to neurons. Q30 Innovations’s technology, alongside other such neuromodulation technologies that function by stimulating nervous system structures, ______ the way for future advancements in neurotechnology.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Moving beyond a simple “present or absent” designation, researchers created a new classification system that allows for a nuanced understanding of bioluminescence in marine organisms that was unavailable under binary classification systems. <u>The new six-point scale considers varying levels of supporting evidence used to identify bioluminescent species.</u> For example, the firefly squid scores 1 because of inconsistent reports, the emperor squid scores 4 because of its anatomical similarity to known luminous relatives, and the shaggy anglerfish scores 6 because of substantiated direct observations.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It emphasizes the thoroughness of the research conducted.
It explains how the new classification system was derived from the previous binary system.
It justifies the need for a new classification system for marine species.
It explains the basis for the new system’s scoring criteria.

question:
Antonia Olivia Dolan and colleagues had musicians and nonmusicians with clinically average hearing listen to recordings of nature sounds and music in popular genres like acoustic folk and funk and adjust the volume to optimize their listening enjoyment. The researchers found that for a given recording that a musician and nonmusician identified as their favorite among those included in the study, optimal volume tended to be higher for the musician than for the nonmusician. Thus, if a musician and nonmusician both identified Jose Gonzalez’s “Heartbeats” as their favorite recording and the musician preferred to listen to it at a volume of 82.2 decibels, the nonmusician would be expected to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: find listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels less enjoyable than listening to it at a lower volume.
prefer listening to other music at 82.2 decibels over listening to “Heartbeats” at that volume.
enjoy listening to the nature sounds at 82.2 decibels more than listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels.
not find it enjoyable to listen to any recordings at a volume as low as 82.2 decibels.

question:
A 2024 study cataloged all the trees in Amsterdam to evaluate the biodiversity of the city’s urban forest. The researchers, finding that administrative unit GK13 had a 0.62 ratio of native to non-native trees, ______ efforts to improve the biodiversity of the trees in that unit and other areas with a similarly moderate ratio.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Scientists have used machine learning tools to study elephant sounds, uncovering a sophisticated communication system. The tools ______ unique patterns in the rumbling sounds elephants make. The scientists claim that these patterns are specific calls the elephants use for individuals, similar to names.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

Seventeenth-century Flemish artist Clara Peeters played a crucial role in the history of still-life painting. At a time when historical paintings were the preferred genre—indeed, at a time when there wasn’t even a term for still-life painting in Peeters’s language—Peeters painted food, flowers, fish, and game. Her influence spread throughout Western Europe and she became so strongly associated with the genre that painters who took up similar subjects were sometimes described as belonging to the “circle of Peeters.”

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Clara Peeters was an important figure in the development of still-life painting.
Clara Peeters made significant contributions to multiple genres of painting.
Clara Peeters introduced the term “still-life painting” to Western Europe.
Some paintings attributed to Clara Peeters may have been painted by other artists in her circle.
explanation:
Logic: The passage explains that Clara Peeters helped establish still-life painting as an important artistic genre and influenced later painters. The main idea is her significance to the genre.

Correct: A. Clara Peeters was an important figure in the development of still-life painting.

Incorrect B. The passage discusses only still-life painting, not multiple genres.

Incorrect C. It specifically states there was not even a term for still-life painting in her language.

Incorrect D. The "circle of Peeters" refers to her influence, not uncertainty about authorship.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The human tongue contains taste receptors for a rich, savory flavor called umami.
• Umami is triggered by the compounds in a variety of foods, including sardines and mushrooms.
• Participants in a study tasted a sample of wakame, a type of brown seaweed.
• They rated its umami intensity as moderate.
• The participants tasted a sample of ma-konbu, another type of brown seaweed.
• They rated its umami intensity as high.
The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two seaweeds. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: While wakame and ma-konbu contain umami flavor, umami can also be found in sardines and mushrooms.
After tasting two types of brown seaweed, wakame and ma-konbu, participants in a study found ma-konbu’s umami flavor to be the more intense of the two.
Wakame is a type of brown seaweed, but so is ma-konbu.
Some types of brown seaweed, like wakame and ma-konbu, trigger umami flavor in human taste buds.
explanation:
Logic: The student wants to emphasize the difference between wakame and ma-konbu, specifically their differing umami intensity.

Correct: B. This choice directly compares the two seaweeds and states that ma-konbu has the stronger umami flavor.

Incorrect A. It discusses foods containing umami instead of comparing the seaweeds.

Incorrect C. It focuses on a similarity rather than a difference.

Incorrect D. It explains what both seaweeds have in common rather than contrasting them.

question:
The following text is adapted from Edith Wharton’s 1911 novella Ethan Frome. The narrator has asked the woman he rents a room from about Ethan Frome, a town resident he encountered recently.

Her mind was a store-house of innocuous anecdote and any question about her acquaintances brought forth a volume of detail; but on the subject of Ethan Frome I found her unexpectedly reticent. There was no hint of disapproval in her <u>reserve</u>; I merely felt in her an insurmountable reluctance to speak of him.

As used in the text, what does the word “reserve” most nearly mean?
explanation:
Logic: The narrator says the woman was reluctant to discuss Ethan Frome. Here, reserve means restraint in speaking.

Correct: B. constraint — Constraint means restraint or inhibition, matching her reluctance to speak.

Incorrect A. misgiving — Misgiving means doubt or suspicion, which is not expressed.

Incorrect C. composure — Composure means calmness rather than reluctance.

Incorrect D. modesty — Modesty means humility and does not fit the context.

question:
Archaeologist Weiwei Wang and her colleagues analyzed footed grinding slabs and other food-preparation tools excavated from Óc Eo, a Southeast Asian port city that flourished between the first and sixth centuries CE. Wang and colleagues recovered microscopic remnants of turmeric and other spices from the surfaces of the tools. Turmeric is native to South Asia, more than a thousand miles west of Óc Eo, and the researchers showed that the footed grinding slabs at Óc Eo are very similar to footed grinding slabs common throughout South Asia from around 500 BCE to 300 CE. Wang and colleagues’ findings therefore indicate that there must have been a trade link, whether direct or indirect, between the two regions.

Which finding, if true, would directly weaken the conclusion about Wang and her colleagues’ findings that is presented in the text?
choices: Other types of artifacts originating in South Asia and dating to the first through sixth centuries CE have been found throughout Southeast Asia.
In the first through third centuries CE, there was a significant migration of people from South Asia to Southeast Asia.
The people of Óc Eo and several communities in South Asia regularly traded with people in the region that is now the southeast Asian country of Malaysia no later than the first century CE.
Some of the spices recovered from Óc Eo are native to the Maluku Islands, which are located approximately 2,000 miles southeast of Óc Eo.
explanation:
Logic: The conclusion claims trade links existed between South Asia and Óc Eo. A competing explanation would weaken that conclusion.

Correct: B. Migration from South Asia could explain the presence of spices and tools without requiring trade.

Incorrect A. Finding additional South Asian artifacts strengthens the trade explanation.

Incorrect C. Trading through Malaysia still supports indirect trade between the regions.

Incorrect D. Spices from the Maluku Islands do not undermine evidence of South Asian trade.

question:
Last-mile delivery refers to the final step in delivering packages to customers—and this final step can be very difficult. Delivery companies are contending with the increasing popularity of next-day delivery and with the increasing volume of parcels to be delivered, resulting in a growing bottleneck of packages in the last-mile delivery stage. These companies have been experimenting with innovative solutions in last-mile delivery, including self-service lockers (containers where consumers can pick up their parcels using a unique code). Unfortunately, many of these innovations create new obstacles (e.g., convenient placement of self-service lockers is challenging) and are not ready for full-scale implementation. As a result, delivery companies will likely _____

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: encourage consumers to expect next-day delivery only for products that are widely available.
continue to struggle with last-mile delivery operations until viable solutions become available.
be able to meet consumers’ expectations for next-day delivery in many areas but not in all regions.
have little incentive to find a solution to last-mile delivery challenges.
explanation:
Logic: The passage explains that current innovations are not yet sufficient to solve last-mile delivery challenges. Companies will therefore continue facing those problems.

Correct: B. Delivery companies will likely continue struggling until practical large-scale solutions become available.

Incorrect A. The passage never suggests limiting next-day delivery based on product availability.

Incorrect C. The passage does not compare different regions.

Incorrect D. The companies clearly have strong incentives to solve the problem.

question:
Across brown bears—omnivores with high dietary plasticity—there is wide variety in dietary mix, which may reflect genetics, local resource availability, or social learning (cubs stay with their mothers for two years or more). Evaluating these possibilities, Anne Hertel et al. analyzed 30 years of data on trophic position (indicative of dietary mix) for female brown bears. After separation, daughters, who tended to settle near their mothers, occupied the same trophic positions as their mothers for two years, but the correlation disappeared by year five. Trophic correlation with unrelated individuals in similar habitats was modest, while habitat-independent correlation with nonmaternal relatives (e.g., cousins) was no different than with unrelated individuals. These findings suggest that _____

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: social learning and resource fluctuations may both play a role in dietary mix among females, at least temporarily, though genetic factors appear to make a significant contribution as well.
female dietary mix is best understood as changeable and contingent on fluctuating environmental conditions rather than as the result of social learning or genetic factors.
dietary mix among females may reflect a social learning effect that eventually diminishes, though environmental constraints cannot be ruled out as a contributing factor.

growing dissimilarity between mothers and their daughters with regard to dietary mix may reflect changes in the resources available in maternal habitats, though social learning could also contribute to the trend.
explanation:
Logic: Mother-daughter similarities disappear over time, suggesting a temporary social-learning effect, while genetics receive little support and environmental effects remain possible.

Correct: C. The findings suggest social learning fades over time, although environmental influences cannot be ruled out.

Incorrect A. The study provides little evidence that genetics make a significant contribution.

Incorrect B. The temporary mother-daughter similarity supports a role for social learning.

Incorrect D. The study does not show that changing maternal habitats explain the growing differences.

question:
Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey (1818) is considered a satire of another novel popular at the time: Ann Radcliffe’s The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794), which Austen’s heroine, Catherine Morland, is depicted reading. However, the similarity of the _____ experiences—the predicaments of both Catherine and Radcliffe’s Emily St. Aubert result from men’s greed—suggests that underlying the satire is a social critique.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

To determine the approximate age of stone tools excavated from ancient lake beds in Saudi Arabia, archaeologist Eleanor Scerri and colleagues collected samples of sediments surrounding the tools; these samples were then analyzed using a method known as optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. _____ OSL dating indicated that the tools were around 400,000 years old.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The first sentence describes the process of dating the tools. The second sentence gives the final result of that process.

Correct: D. Ultimately, — Ultimately correctly signals the final outcome of the dating procedure.

Incorrect A. In addition merely adds information rather than indicating the final result.

Incorrect B. By comparison suggests a comparison that is not present.

Incorrect C. Similarly indicates similarity rather than sequence.

question:
The moon Lysithea orbits Jupiter in the same direction that the planet rotates. _____ Lysithea’s orbit is described as prograde. Mneme, another of Jupiter’s moons, orbits in the opposite direction, so its orbit is described with the opposite term: retrograde.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: Lysithea orbits in the same direction as Jupiter's rotation, so its orbit is therefore called prograde.

Correct: C. Thus, — Thus correctly signals the conclusion drawn from the preceding fact.

Incorrect A. Likewise compares similar ideas rather than showing cause and effect.

Incorrect B. Next indicates sequence, which is not intended.

Incorrect D. However incorrectly signals contrast.

question:
Macarena Garcia Marin is a space scientist who works on the James Webb Space Telescope, or JWST. Thanks in part to Garcia Marin’s contributions, the telescope is now positioned near the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, almost one million miles beyond Earth’s orbit. _____ the JWST’s predecessor, the Hubble Telescope, is only about 340 miles above Earth’s surface.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The JWST is almost one million miles beyond Earth's orbit, whereas Hubble is only about 340 miles above Earth. The transition should signal contrast.

Correct: C. By contrast, — By contrast appropriately highlights the difference in location.

Incorrect A. Similarly incorrectly suggests similarity.

Incorrect B. Secondly introduces a sequence rather than a comparison.

Incorrect D. Therefore incorrectly suggests cause and effect.

question:
Nineteenth-century Modernista architects championed nature in their designs. Granted, the wavy stone façade and ornate floral tilework of Casa Batlló, a Modernista private home designed by Antoni Gaudí, couldn’t exactly grow in a forest. _____ one sees natural influences in Gaudí’s penchant for curves (rather than right angles) and plant- and animal-inspired flourishes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The first sentence admits the building is not literally natural, while the next explains that it is still inspired by nature. The transition should indicate concession.

Correct: C. Still, — Still correctly signals that the natural inspiration exists despite the previous concession.

Incorrect A. Furthermore simply adds information without acknowledging the contrast.

Incorrect B. Similarly incorrectly indicates comparison.

Incorrect C. In other words restates rather than contrasts the previous idea.

question:
For millennia, acorns were a staple food for the Tongva people, the Indigenous inhabitants of what is now the Los Angeles basin. Raw acorns have an extremely bitter taste, though, due to their high tannin levels. ______ it was necessary to process the acorns—which involved grinding, rinsing, and shaping the nuts into a dough—before eating them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: Because raw acorns were extremely bitter, processing them before eating was necessary; the relationship is cause and effect.

A. However — Incorrect: The second sentence does not contrast with the bitterness.
B. Afterward — Incorrect: The passage emphasizes consequence, not merely chronological order.
C. Similarly — Incorrect: No similar situation is being compared.
D. Therefore — Correct: The bitterness caused the need for processing.

question:
It’s tempting to think that the comic strips Jump Start and Wee Pals have the same main purpose—to amuse—because both feature humorous situations. ______ Wee Pals focuses just as much on challenging readers with sociopolitical commentary as it does on making them laugh.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The first sentence presents a tempting belief, while the second corrects that belief by explaining Wee Pals’ additional sociopolitical purpose.

A. In other words — Incorrect: The second sentence does not restate the first.
B. Likewise — Incorrect: The second sentence does not present a similar idea.
C. Next — Incorrect: The relationship is not chronological.
D. In reality — Correct: It signals that the actual situation differs from the initial assumption.

question:
Readers sometimes divide the works of twentieth-century English author Evelyn Waugh into two periods: one consisting of his early satirical novels and the other consisting of his later, more serious—even ponderous—books. Critic Seamus Perry, however, challenges that strict division. Perry argues that Waugh’s writing didn’t change over time as much as some readers have suggested. For instance, Perry contends that some of Waugh’s earliest works, notably his biography of artist Dante Gabriel Rossetti, exhibit the earnest romanticism that would characterize Waugh’s later fiction.

Based on the text, which statement about Waugh’s works would Perry most likely agree with?
choices: Regardless of when they were written, Waugh’s works have important similarities that transcend their differences.
Over time, Waugh’s works became less humorous and more focused on weightier topics.
Waugh’s works can appropriately be separated into two periods by their subject matter and tone.
The earliest of Waugh’s works exhibit a satirical tone, even if that tone is more apparent in Waugh’s later works.
explanation:
Logic: Perry argues Waugh's works are more consistent across his career than critics believe, pointing to serious qualities already present in his early writing.

A. Correct: Perry believes important similarities exist across Waugh's works regardless of when they were written.
B. Incorrect: This is the view Perry rejects.
C. Incorrect: Perry specifically challenges the strict two-period division.
D. Incorrect: Perry says early works already contained later characteristics, not that later works became more satirical.

question:
When it was built in the nineteenth century, the Eiffel Tower was criticized—even protested—for its unique appearance. ______ the spire-like structure earned not just acceptance but adoration, and its iconic design is now echoed in everything from the Eiffel Tower replica in Klagenfurt, Austria, to the Tokyo Tower in Tokyo, Japan.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The passage describes how opinions changed over time—from criticism when the Eiffel Tower was built to admiration later.

A. Incorrect: The second sentence is not an example of the first.
B. Incorrect: The admiration did not occur as a direct logical consequence.
C. Correct: "Ultimately" signals the final outcome after the passage of time.
D. Incorrect: "Similarly" indicates similarity rather than change.

question:
Visiting flowers that produce high volumes of nectar allows hummingbirds, including stripe-throated hermits, to maximize their foraging efficiency. But nectar can’t be seen from outside the flower, and while <u>some studies have suggested that petal length may indicate nectar volume</u>, María A. Maglianesi and team found no such association among hummingbird-visited plants at Los Cusingos Bird Sanctuary and other sites in Costa Rica. The researchers hypothesize that by driving hummingbirds to visit more plants in search of high-reward flowers, plants’ lack of reliable signaling may increase chances of pollination.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices: It attributes the inconclusive findings reported in the text regarding the influence of a particular floral trait on interactions between hummingbirds and plants to differences in study sites.

It suggests that a hypothesis discussed later in the text regarding a potential visual cue that hummingbirds rely on to increase their foraging efficiency has little support from the broader scientific community.

It acknowledges research findings, which weren’t replicated by the study discussed later in the text, positing a relationship between floral traits that potentially underlies hummingbird foraging decisions.
It summarizes contradictory study findings concerning a floral trait that influences hummingbird foraging patterns, which the study mentioned later in the text aimed to resolve.
explanation:
Logic: The underlined sentence introduces earlier research suggesting petal length predicts nectar volume, which the new study later fails to confirm.

A. Incorrect: Site differences are never identified as the cause.
B. Incorrect: The passage doesn't evaluate broader scientific support.
C. Correct: It presents earlier findings that the later study does not replicate.
D. Incorrect: The later study wasn't designed specifically to resolve conflicting findings.

question:
Nineteenth-century Modernista architects championed nature in their designs. Granted, the wavy stone facade and ornate floral tilework of Casa Batlló, a Modernista private home designed by Antoni Gaudí, couldn’t exactly grow in a forest. ______ one sees natural influences in Gaudí’s penchant for curves (rather than right angles) and plant- and animal-inspired flourishes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The sentence first admits Casa Batlló couldn't literally grow in nature, then contrasts that idea by pointing out its natural inspirations.

A. Incorrect: "Similarly" indicates similarity rather than contrast.
B. Incorrect: "Furthermore" simply adds information.
C. Correct: "Still" introduces a concession that contrasts with the previous sentence.
D. Incorrect: "In other words" restates rather than contrasts.

question:
Ancient Athens had a unique form of governing called direct democracy that allowed all citizens to gather, speak, and vote personally on government decisions. ______ citizens of modern countries usually elect representatives to make laws on their behalf because modern countries’ populations are too large for direct democracy to be practical.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: Ancient Athens used direct democracy, whereas modern countries usually use representative democracy. The relationship is contrast.

A. Incorrect: The two systems are not similar.
B. Correct: "By contrast" correctly signals the difference.
C. Incorrect: "Additionally" merely adds another point.
D. Incorrect: The second sentence is not an example of the first.

question:
A recent study found that groups of Paratrechina longicornis ants solved a geometric puzzle more efficiently than human groups. While humans performed well as individuals because of strategic thinking, working in teams did not enhance humans’ problem-solving efficiency. ______ as part of a closely connected colony, the ants effectively used shared memory and coordination, collectively solving a problem that no ant could have solved alone.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: Humans perform well individually but not in groups, whereas ants become more effective when working together. The relationship is contrast.

A. Incorrect: The second sentence doesn't simply add information.
B. Incorrect: Humans and ants behave differently, not similarly.
C. Incorrect: The second sentence isn't a consequence of the first.
D. Correct: Conversely signals the opposite pattern.

question:
• Throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, populations of Black Americans increased in many cities throughout the state of New York.
• During this time, many Black newspapers were founded.
• The newspapers were largely by and for the Black communities in which they were based.
• The New York Citizen-Call ran from 1960 to 1961 in New York City, New York.
• The Syracuse Gazette ran from 1976 to 1980 in Syracuse, New York.
Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize the geographic similarities between the two newspapers?
choices: From 1960 to 1961, the New York Citizen-Call served the Black community of New York City, New York, as did the Syracuse Gazette.

The New York Citizen-Call and the Syracuse Gazette, both based in New York, are among the many Black newspapers that sprung up in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to provide a voice to the growing Black communities throughout the state.
The New York Citizen-Call was one of many Black newspapers to spring up in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, debuting in 1960 and later followed by the Syracuse Gazette in 1976.

The New York Citizen-Call and the Syracuse Gazette were both based in cities within the same state—New York City and Syracuse, respectively—and thus served Black communities in New York rather than in any other state.
explanation:
Logic: The goal is to emphasize that both newspapers were based in New York State, highlighting their shared geography.

A. Incorrect: It incorrectly implies the Syracuse Gazette served New York City.

B. Incorrect: It states that they sprung up to provide a voice to the growing Black communities, which is not found in the text.

C. Incorrect: It focuses mainly on chronology.

D. Correct: It emphasizes that they were in the same state

question:
Solar physicists studying the Sun have identified an important ______ between magnetically active and relatively quiet regions. In active regions, bursts of ultraviolet light usually come before substantial decreases in magnetic energy, whereas in quiet regions, ultraviolet light intensity and magnetic energy remain continuously correlated without notable energy drops.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Logic: The passage contrasts what happens in active versus quiet solar regions, emphasizing their difference.

A. Incorrect: It isn't describing how they interact.
B. Correct: Disparity means an important difference.
C. Incorrect: There is no compromise between the regions.
D. Incorrect: They aren't being compared as similar.

question:
Maya Elena Ruiz and colleagues conducted a study comparing musicians and nonmusicians in the volume, measured in decibels (dB), that they preferred when listening to various audio recordings, including solo piano pieces, symphonic works, and ocean sounds. The musicians, who reported far greater lifetime noise exposure than the nonmusicians, generally listened to the recordings at higher volumes than the nonmusicians did. The two groups had clinically similar hearing, however, suggesting that although a musician’s preferred volume for a favorite recording might be 84.8 dB and a nonmusician’s might be 65.9 dB, this difference ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: indicates that the musician is unlikely to listen to a nonfavorite recording at a higher volume than the nonmusician would.
shows that both the musician and the nonmusician have lower hearing ability than would be expected of clinically typical individuals with typical levels of lifetime noise exposure.
does not arise from the musician having a clinically significant reduction in hearing ability as a result of lifetime noise exposure.
cannot be explained as resulting from the musician’s relatively greater musical expertise.
explanation:
Logic: The two groups have similar hearing, so the musicians' higher preferred volume cannot be explained by hearing loss.

A. Incorrect: The passage doesn't discuss favorite versus nonfavorite recordings.
B. Incorrect: Both groups have clinically similar hearing.
C. Correct: Similar hearing means the difference isn't due to hearing damage.
D. Incorrect: The passage doesn't rule out musical expertise.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A nonnative species that causes environmental or economic harm when introduced to an ecosystem is considered invasive.
• Leafy spurge is an invasive species of flowering plant that crowds out livestock forage and native plants.
• It was first introduced to the US accidentally through contaminated seed.
• Water hyacinth is an invasive species of aquatic plant that blocks sunlight and reduces oxygen levels in bodies of water.
• It was first introduced to the US as an ornamental plant.
The student wants to emphasize a similarity between leafy spurge and water hyacinth. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Water hyacinth is an invasive species that blocks sunlight and reduces oxygen levels in bodies of water, causing environmental harm.
Leafy spurge was first introduced accidentally through contaminated seed, but it now crowds out livestock forage and native plants.
The harm to ecosystems caused by water hyacinth and leafy spurge has led both species to be considered invasive in the US.
Leafy spurge is an invasive species of aquatic plant, and water hyacinth was first introduced accidentally through contaminated seed.
explanation:
Logic: The goal is to emphasize a similarity between leafy spurge and water hyacinth, so the answer should identify what both have in common.

A. Incorrect: It discusses only water hyacinth.
B. Incorrect: It discusses only leafy spurge.
C. Correct: Both species are invasive because they harm ecosystems.
D. Incorrect: It incorrectly swaps facts about the two plants.

question:

• Nandi Khumalo was a South African singer.
• The song “Thula Bane” appears on her 1962 album Nandi Khumalo.

Originally made popular by the Beatles, the song “Here Comes the Sun” appears on Nandi Khumalo’s album Remember Me.

question:
When ordering the branches of the Colville River system, cartographers tend to begin with the riverway’s lowest point, the Colville River. ______ hydrologists begin at the top of the river system, with the Siksikpuk River and other tributaries fed by the riverway’s source, Alaska’s De Long Mountains.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: Cartographers and hydrologists start ordering river branches from opposite ends of the river system, so the relationship is contrast.

A. Incorrect: The methods are opposite, not similar.
B. Incorrect: The second sentence isn't an example.
C. Correct: "By contrast" signals the opposing approaches.
D. Incorrect: The second sentence doesn't restate the first.

question:
Text 1
Good art often challenges and disrupts social and aesthetic norms, but the creation of public art—paintings, sculptures, and performance pieces displayed in nonmuseum or nontheatrical public settings—typically requires broad agreement among artists, civic officials, and community members about the works’ message and artistic goals. <u>Public art that fails to appease everyone by being sufficiently aesthetically and conceptually bland almost inevitably provokes backlash.</u>

Text 2
Public art is commonly displayed in spaces intended for purposes other than meaningful aesthetic engagement. Some critics of public art therefore note that norm-defying pieces that aren’t effectively integrated within their surroundings in a manner that primes passersby to appreciate the pieces’ merits (as is often the case) tend to be regarded more unfavorably than similarly provocative art encountered in museums is.

Based on the texts, how would the critics mentioned in Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined claim in Text 1?
choices: By disputing the notion that civic leaders and community members are easily placated by art that is intended mainly to reinforce social norms
By agreeing with the idea that only works of art that are universally appealing are suitable for displaying in public spaces
By arguing that the reason members of the general public might disagree about a public artwork’s merits is unrelated to the unconventionality of its appearance and ideas
By contending that the kinds of reactions controversial public artworks often receive aren’t exclusively the result of attributes inherent in the works themselves

Text 1
As part of a study of ungulates (hoofed mammals) native to the Yellowstone River basin, fresh dung samples from identified individuals were collected in the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes Bison Range of Montana. Based on steroidal analysis, on average the bison and elk samples had similar levels of beta-sitosterol and stigmastanol, which distinguished these species’ profiles from that of moose.

Although fecal-steroidal profile alone is not sufficient to distinguish between samples from bison and those from elk, the relative levels of zoostanols (steroids with animal origins), such as coprostanol and 24-ethyl-coprostanol, in sediments at Buffalo Ford Lake in Yellowstone National Park show that bison, elk, or both were the predominant ungulates in the lake’s watershed for all strata of sediment examined, going as far back as 2,300 years.

Which conclusion about steroid profiles is supported by information in both Text 1 and Text 2?
choices: The profiles for bison and elk contain similar concentrations of various steroids.
Each of the ungulate species in the Buffalo Ford Lake watershed has a distinctive and unique steroidal profile.
Some steroids in the bison and elk profiles are more likely than others to be preserved for long time spans.
The profiles of ungulates in and around the Yellowstone basin show that bison and elk have historically been more prevalent than moose in the area.

question:
Some representations of the cataclysmic fate of the comic book planet Krypton illustrate a common trope in disaster stories: people’s self-destructive carelessness. Explanations of real-world societal collapse betray a similar pattern. One theory about the downfall of Rapa Nui, for example, argues that residents invited disaster by despoiling the island’s Jubaea palm forests, leading to a scarcity of wood for fuel and canoe construction. Archaeological evidence, however, suggests that residents adapted to environmental conditions by relying on grass and other plants for cooking and driftwood for making canoes. Given that other factors—e.g., disease and conflict arising from European contact—played a crucial role in Rapa Nui’s eventual demise, it therefore seems unlikely that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: deforestation was merely indirectly responsible for an irreversible collapse of Rapa Nui’s subsistence economy.
its residents’ focus on environmental challenges prevented them from devoting adequate attention to political issues.
its residents’ lack of environmental awareness was ultimately responsible for Rapa Nui’s collapse.

For example, if the favorite recording of both a participating musician and a participating nonmusician was Jose Gonzalez’s “Heartbeats” and the musician played it at 84.8 dB, it was therefore likely that ______

Country | Percent change in total production | Percent change in market prices

A tariff is a tax on imported goods intended to protect domestic producers of similar goods from international competition. Eliminating tariffs can lead to an influx of cheaper imported goods, lowering prices; in a place where domestic production is relatively expensive, this influx can suppress domestic production, as the country’s consumers favor more cheaply produced imported goods over domestically produced ones. A student consults a table showing projected changes in production and average market prices of agricultural commodities in four countries in a tariff-elimination scenario. Based on the data, the student claims that compared with China and Russia, agricultural production in Argentina and Canada is likely relatively inexpensive.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the text and data from the table to support the student’s claim?
choices: Although eliminating tariffs would likely cause agricultural market prices to decrease in most locations, it would likely cause agricultural market prices to increase in both Argentina and Canada.
Argentina and Canada are the only countries shown that are projected to see both an increase in agricultural production and a reduction in agricultural prices in the absence of tariffs.
In the absence of tariffs, total agricultural production in Argentina and Canada would likely exceed that in China and Russia.
Although agricultural production in China and Russia would likely decrease if tariffs were eliminated, it would likely increase in both Argentina and Canada.

High entropy alloys (HEAs) typically combine five or more elements in roughly equal proportions, and medium entropy alloys (MEAs) typically combine three or four elements in similar proportions. HEAs and MEAs are known for withstanding cracking at extremely low (cryogenic) temperatures relatively well, though their fracture toughness generally falls as temperature does. Dong Liu et al. investigated the fracture toughness (both the initiation and propagation toughness) of the HEA CrMnFeCoNi and its MEA derivative CrCoNi and concluded that the alloys’ toughness performance differs from that of most HEAs and MEAs.

Which choice best describes data in the graph that support Liu et al.’s conclusion?
choices: For both CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi, initiation toughness and propagation toughness were lower at 293 kelvins than at 20 kelvins.
The changes in initiation toughness and propagation toughness were greater between 20 kelvins and 77 kelvins than between 77 kelvins and 198 kelvins for both CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi.
CrCoNi outperformed CrMnFeCoNi at 20 kelvins in both initiation toughness and propagation toughness even though it is composed of fewer elements.
Both CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi showed substantially higher propagation toughness than initiation toughness throughout the range from 20 kelvins to 293 kelvins.

question:
A creole language is an amalgam of a lexifier, or primary contributor of grammar and vocabulary, with one or more substrates, or secondary contributors. English-lexifying creoles in North America, such as Afro-Seminole Creole, rely on West African substrates, while Hawaiian Pidgin relies on ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, the Polynesian language of the Native Hawaiian people, with further contributions from Korean and other East Asian languages, Portuguese, and Spanish. This is a heterogeneous history, even for a creole language. Moreover, numerous similarities are found among the East Asian substrates, as well as between Portuguese and Spanish. Thus, it can be challenging to credit certain words or features of grammar or pronunciation to any one substrate.

Which statement, if true, would best illustrate the challenge described in the text?
choices: As is also the case with some first-language speakers of Afro-Seminole Creole, many first-language speakers of Hawaiian Pidgin align their pronunciation, word choice, and syntax more closely with English in certain conversational contexts than in others.

Stative structures in which verbs modify subjects and serve a descriptive function comparable to that of adjectives are hallmarks of Hawaiian Pidgin as well as of East Asian languages such as Korean, yet the syntax of Hawaiian Pidgin’s stative structures confirms their origin in ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi.

Hawaiian Pidgin’s substitution of “d” for the voiced “th” consonant (as used in “that”) and of “t” for the unvoiced “th” consonant (as used in “thick”) can be credited to the absence of “th” consonants in ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, though most other Polynesian languages lack “th” consonants too.

The usage of the Hawaiian Pidgin verb “ste” to convey a temporary state, as in the statement “da watah ste cold” (the water is cold), most nearly resembles that of the ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi verb noho, though the Portuguese verb ficar and the Spanish verb estar have similar usages and may also exert an influence on “ste.”

question:
Blandine Courel and her colleagues analyzed pottery fragments from thirty-five sites across the Volga and Don river basins to determine whether the ways in which hunter-gatherer societies used pottery in these regions around 6,500–8,000 years ago were influenced primarily by local food availability or primarily by cultural factors. Analysis of organic residues on the pottery fragments showed different prevailing uses for pottery in these locations—cooking and storing terrestrial animal protein at Volga sites and cooking and storing aquatic animal protein at Don sites—which Courel and colleagues attribute to cultural differences.

Assuming that the Volga and Don basins supported similarly sized hunter-gatherer populations 6,500–8,000 years ago, which finding, if true, would most directly support Courel and colleagues’ explanation?
choices: The people of the Volga basin acquired the techniques used to create pottery for cooking and storing food from the people of the Don basin.
Across the Volga and Don basins, people had broadly similar access to the same terrestrial and aquatic animal resources.
There were many more bodies of water in a comparably sized area in the Don basin than in the Volga basin.
In both the Volga and Don basins, most of the sites from which pottery has been recovered appear to have been seasonal fishing and hunting encampments rather than year-round settlements.
